# The trace command: mismatch handling and error paths, never an unhandled exception
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #168, sha256:e33f0c245905e5ed6eba1d9dd0ba6f5a292b9d8556c92129718aae09cb6c2fde). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Done 2026-10-29 (six named tests, trace handles mismatches and bad inputs; CI green on 8a31e96; Decider D117; follow-ups in card 172)
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** tooling (thin slice; split from card 161 by Decider D113)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Decider D113 (2026-10-28): card 161 closes on its core outcome and the remaining review findings become small separate cards, each reviewable and revertable on its own. Two independent reviews of card 161 asked for this work.
- **Depends on:** 161
- **Story:** As Morgan, I want phrase trace to handle every bad input with a clear message, so that tracing a failure never crashes and a stale map is never trusted silently.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a build, When phrase trace runs with --assembly, Then a matching assembly prints a matching build check, and an assembly built from a different source prints a loud warning that is nonzero with --strict and zero without; a changed generated file reports a csHash mismatch
  2. Given a name, When it is a Class.Method frame taken from the map, or a name shared by several records, Then the right record is found, and shared names print every match
  3. Given bad inputs, When the map is invalid JSON, has null records or a missing field, is missing, or the assembly path is bad, Then trace prints what is wrong and exits nonzero without an unhandled exception (the map is validated after parsing)

## Context

- This closes the unproven part of card 161's second criterion. Follow docs/CODING_GUIDELINES.md: one required test per criterion, shown failing first; the generated C# output stays identical (the recorded orders hash stays 409bf3c6...).
